is_anopheles.evidence: Studies Anopheles coluzzii and Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes collected in central Côte d'Ivoire (Page 1, Abstract; Page 3, 'Species identification').

reports_target_markers.evidence: Mosquitoes were genotyped for Vgsc L1014F (L995F) and Ace-1 G119S (G280S) mutations using TaqMan qPCR assays (Page 4, 'Detection of Kdr L1014F mutation in An. gambiae s.l.' and 'Detection of Ace-1R G119S mutation in An. gambiae s.l.').

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Genotypic (RR, RS, SS) and allelic counts and frequencies are reported in Table 1 (page 5), Table 2 (page 6), and Table 3 (page 7) for both An. coluzzii and An. gambiae.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were field-collected as adults by human landing catches (HLC) from 40 villages around Bouaké in central Côte d'Ivoire between May 2017 and April 2019 (Page 1, Abstract; Page 3, 'Study area' and 'Mosquito collection and processing').

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical research article testing field-caught An. gambiae s.l. mosquitoes for Plasmodium infection and insecticide resistance markers.

sub_country_location.evidence: Collected in 40 villages within a 60-km radius in the district of Bouaké, central Côte d'Ivoire (Page 3, 'Study area').

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected over a 2-year window from May 2017 to April 2019 (Page 1, Abstract; Page 3, 'Study area').

duplicate_risk.evidence: Mosquitoes were sampled as part of a larger cluster-randomized controlled trial: 'The methodology used in this study has been well described by Sternberg et al. [25]. Briefly, 40 villages within a 60-km radius in the district of Bouaké were identified for inclusion in the study' (Page 3).

supplement.evidence: Full genotype and allele count data per species, trial arm, and infection status are provided in Tables 1, 2, and 3 in the main text.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated wild Anopheles gambiae and An. coluzzii collected across 40 villages around Bouaké, Côte d'Ivoire between May 2017 and April 2019. A total of 1255 mosquitoes were successfully identified to sibling species and genotyped for Vgsc L1014F and Ace-1 G119S, with genotype counts provided overall, by trial arm, and by Plasmodium infection status.
